title: Name the day's best-selling product

blocks.text: The shop's morning e-mail names yesterday's best-selling product: the one with the most units over all of the day's order lines. A product can appear on any number of lines, anywhere in the day. A busy day has tens of millions of lines, so the count has been given a `ForkJoinPool` and a threshold.
Write `top` in `src/main/java/practice/BestSeller.java`, with the `RecursiveTask` it runs as a nested class. When you're done:

items: `top` returns the product with the most units, and how many it sold, for any threshold;
when two products sold the same number of units, the smaller product id wins.

blocks.text: About twenty-five lines in total, most of them the task class. The tests run `BestSeller` on a pool of three workers, with days of 1 to about 3,000 order lines.

cases.says: top names the product with the most units and its total, for one line, a short day with a tie, and a long day at several thresholds
a product that leads no stretch of lines but sells the most over the day is the best seller, whatever the threshold

origin.section: The Parent Can Only Combine What Its Halves Return

concepts: The value a task returns must hold enough to combine with its sibling's so that any split gives the answer one task would: sets for a distinct count, sum and count for an average, every value's count for the most frequent one.
